_comment: Shared, tracked permissions for pybers. Machine-specific grants would live in
settings.local.json (gitignored); there is none, and nothing here needs one yet.
PRINCIPLE: read-only tools, plus THIS REPO'S OWN SCRIPTS BY NAME,
and only their read-only subcommands. Nothing that grants arbitrary execution.
‼ A permission string is matched as TEXT. A grant reading `python` where every command is
written `python3` matches nothing, and every run prompts anyway. A permission that never fires is worse than none, because it reads as
covered. So: invoke tests as `.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest`, never `source .venv/bin/activate
&& python -m pytest`, and keep the grant below identical to the invocation.
REMOVED 2026-08-24, described rather than quoted, because a permission-shaped string sitting
in a permissions file is one careless copy-paste from being live again:
· unscoped WebFetch — read-only, but 'any URL, ever'. Scoped by domain below instead.
· a bare pytest grant — pytest is not on PATH outside the venv, so it never fired.
· a .venv/bin/python (no 3) pytest grant — the mismatch described above.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, so they prompt every time. These mutate GitHub or the repo's committed
generated code, and prompting is the correct behavior — NOT denying, which would stop the
skills that legitimately need them:
ticket.py create/edit/start/status/close/block, pr.py create/ready/merge,
protos-extract.py --write.

NOT A SANDBOX. Any of these can be redirected with > and thereby write. The grants exist to remove friction on reading, not to make execution safe — the same assumption the sibling repos make. Anything that mutates deliberately is absent from this list and prompts.
NARROWED 2026-09-01, three grants that read as read-only and were not. The distinction that
decided each one: the paragraph above knowingly accepts a tool that can write only when a
caller adds a redirection. It does not accept a tool that mutates on its own with no
redirection anywhere, which is what these three could do.
· `git branch:*` also covered `git branch -D` and `-m`, deleting and renaming branches.
Replaced by the three read-only forms the skills actually use.
· `sed:*` also covered `sed -i`, editing a file in place. Replaced by `sed -n`, which is
the printing form and the only one used here.
· `find:*` also covered `-delete`, `-exec` and `-ok`. There is no prefix that excludes
them, because the flags follow the path, so the grant is gone entirely. Glob is the
tool for finding files and is already granted.
`awk` and `xxd` stay: both write only through an explicit redirection, which is the case the
paragraph above already accepts.
